title: Maximum Product of Two Elements in an Array
spaceBreakdown:
- int first, int second: two scalar variables → O(1)
- no containers, no recursion, no heap
- not counted: input vector
approach: The maximum of (nums[i]-1)*(nums[j]-1) is achieved by the two largest elements in the array: subtracting 1 preserves ordering, and the product of two positive numbers grows when both factors increase. Track the top two values in a single pass using two variables, then return (largest-1)*(secondLargest-1).
hints: If you fix one of the two chosen elements, what property should the other element have to make the product (nums[i]-1)*(nums[j]-1) as large as possible?
Track the two largest values in a single pass using two variables. For [3,4,5,2]: after processing all elements, first=5 and second=4, giving (5-1)*(4-1)=12.

**Descending order** - the largest element appears first, so the second-largest never triggers the "new max" branch.
`Input: nums = [7,3]` → `Expected: 12`
⚠️ Bug: only updating `second` inside the `if (x > first)` block (no else-if) → second stays 0 → returns (7-1)*(0-1) = -6

**Duplicates** - two equal largest values; the second copy must still update `second`.
`Input: nums = [1,5,4,5]` → `Expected: 16`
⚠️ Bug: using strict `>` with no else-if → second stays 1 → returns (5-1)*(1-1) = 0

**All equal** - every element is identical, so `second` is only set via the `>=` branch.
`Input: nums = [3,3,3]` → `Expected: 4`
⚠️ Bug: using strict `>` with no else-if → second stays 0 → returns (3-1)*(0-1) = -2

followUps.q: What if you must choose k elements (k ≥ 2) and maximize the product of (nums[i]-1) over all chosen indices?
followUps.a: Maintain a min-heap of size k holding the k largest values seen so far. For each element, push it and pop the smallest if the heap exceeds size k. At the end, multiply (value-1) for all k elements in the heap. Time O(n log k), space O(k).

followUps.q: What if nums[i] can be negative (range -10^3 to 10^3)?
followUps.a: The maximum product of two factors can come from either the two largest values or the two smallest (most negative) values, since a negative times a negative is positive. Track the top two and bottom two in a single pass, then compare (max1-1)*(max2-1) versus (min1-1)*(min2-1). Time O(n), space O(1).

followUps.q: What if the array arrives as an unbounded stream and you cannot store all elements?
followUps.a: Keep just two variables (largest and second-largest) updated per incoming element - exactly the current approach. Each element is processed once and discarded, so time is O(n) and space is O(1) regardless of stream length.
